question.text: Capstone scenario — Saptarishi Capital Cat II AIF: Commitment INR 400 cr (fully called), tenure 5 yr, Hurdle 8% compounded, Incentive 20% with 100% catch-up, Terminal NAV INR 700 cr. Compute GP CARRY (approx, in INR crore).

explanation.text: The Logic: Using the workbook's Example 6.5 target-share method for 100% catch-up: the GP's pre-determined share equals the incentive-fee percentage applied to TOTAL profit. Total profit = INR 700 - 400 = INR 300 cr. GP carry target = 20% x INR 300 cr = INR 60 crore, matching keyed option A. Hurdle NAV Y5 = INR 400 x (1.08)^5 = INR 587.73 cr (preferred return INR 187.73 cr), and residual above hurdle = INR 112.27 cr is more than enough to fully catch the GP up to its INR 60 cr target. The Trap: B applies 20% to a wrong base; C computes 20% only on the residual without catch-up; D is an arbitrary figure. Note: Rewrote the explanation to apply Example 6.5's target-share method cleanly and removed the contradictory INR 70.45 crore post-catch-up split, the Cross-Exam Context paragraph, and the LP-deck pro-tip, since those go beyond the source illustration on pp.126-128.
